questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: Which is the basic unit of classification in the taxonomic hierarchy?
questions.explanation: A species is the lowest and basic category of the taxonomic hierarchy; groups of related species form a genus.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: The system of giving each organism a two-part scientific name was introduced by
questions.explanation: Carolus Linnaeus popularised binomial nomenclature, in which a name has a genus part and a species part.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: In the scientific name Mangifera indica Linn., the word 'Linn.' indicates
options: the author who first described the species
the place where the species was found
questions.explanation: The author's name, often abbreviated, is written after the species name; Linn. stands for Linnaeus.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: In the five kingdom classification of Whittaker, unicellular eukaryotic organisms such as Amoeba and Paramecium are placed in kingdom
questions.explanation: Kingdom Protista includes unicellular eukaryotes such as protozoans, diatoms and dinoflagellates.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: Which of the following lists the taxonomic categories correctly from the highest to the lowest rank?
options: Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Order, Genus, Family, Species
Phylum, Kingdom, Class, Family, Order, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Phylum, Order, Class, Family, Genus, Species
questions.explanation: The standard hierarchy is Kingdom, Phylum (Division in plants), Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: A microbiologist finds a unicellular organism with no nuclear membrane, 70S ribosomes and a cell wall containing peptidoglycan. It should be placed in kingdom
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes with peptidoglycan cell walls are bacteria, which belong to kingdom Monera.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: State any two rules followed while writing the scientific name of an organism.
questions.answer: The name is in Latin and printed in italics (underlined separately when handwritten); the genus name starts with a capital letter and the species name with a small letter.
keyPoints: Latin names, italicised or underlined separately
Genus name begins with a capital letter
Species name begins with a small letter
questions.explanation: These are the conventions of binomial nomenclature.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: Why are viruses not included in the five kingdom classification?
questions.answer: Viruses are non-cellular and show characters of life only inside a host cell, where they multiply as obligate parasites; outside the host they behave like non-living particles, so they do not fit any kingdom.
keyPoints: Obligate parasites that multiply only in host cells
Behave as non-living outside the host
questions.explanation: The five kingdom system classifies cellular organisms only.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The pigment that gives brown algae their characteristic colour is
questions.explanation: Brown algae (Phaeophyceae) contain the xanthophyll fucoxanthin in large amounts.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Mosses and liverworts belong to the group
questions.explanation: Bryophytes include liverworts and mosses and are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: In pteridophytes such as ferns, the dominant independent phase of the life cycle is the
questions.explanation: The main plant body of a fern is the diploid sporophyte; the gametophyte is a small prothallus.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Gymnosperms are said to have 'naked seeds' because their
options: ovules are not enclosed within an ovary wall
questions.explanation: In gymnosperms the ovules lie exposed on the megasporophylls, so seeds are not enclosed in fruits.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A plant has vascular tissues and motile male gametes that need water for fertilisation, but it produces no seeds. It most likely belongs to
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes have xylem and phloem and swimming antherozoids but reproduce by spores, not seeds.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: In a haplontic life cycle, the only diploid stage is the
questions.explanation: In haplontic algae such as Spirogyra, the zygote undergoes meiosis and the main body is haploid.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Distinguish between bryophytes and pteridophytes in terms of the dominant phase of their life cycle.
questions.answer: In bryophytes the dominant phase is the haploid gametophyte, with a dependent sporophyte; in pteridophytes the dominant phase is the independent diploid sporophyte, and the gametophyte is small.
keyPoints: Bryophyte sporophyte depends on the gametophyte
questions.explanation: The change in dominant phase is a major trend in plant evolution.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Why do bryophytes remain small and grow in moist places?
questions.answer: They lack true vascular tissues to carry water and food over long distances, and their male gametes swim in water to reach the egg, so they need moist surroundings.
keyPoints: Water needed for fertilisation by swimming gametes
Absorb water directly through the surface
questions.explanation: Absence of conducting tissue limits height, and fertilisation depends on water.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Animals with a spiny skin and a water vascular system belong to phylum
questions.explanation: Echinoderms such as starfish and sea urchins have spiny endoskeletons and a water vascular system.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which phylum is acoelomate, having no body cavity?
questions.explanation: Flatworms such as Taenia and Fasciola have a solid body without a coelom.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which of these animals has an open circulatory system?
questions.explanation: Arthropods like the cockroach have an open circulatory system with blood flowing into body spaces.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Collar cells called choanocytes line the body cavity of
questions.explanation: Choanocytes with flagella create the water current in sponges (Porifera).

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A land vertebrate has dry skin covered with scales, lays shelled eggs on land and is cold-blooded. It belongs to class
questions.explanation: Reptiles have scaly dry skin, lay shelled eggs and are poikilothermic.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A marine animal shows radial symmetry, tissue-level organisation and stinging cells called cnidoblasts. Its phylum is
questions.explanation: Cnidoblasts (cnidocytes) are characteristic of Cnidaria such as Hydra and jellyfish.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Differentiate between diploblastic and triploblastic animals with one example each.
questions.answer: Diploblastic animals have two germ layers, ectoderm and endoderm (e.g. Hydra); triploblastic animals have a third layer, mesoderm, between them (e.g. earthworm or human).
keyPoints: Triploblastic: three germ layers with mesoderm
questions.explanation: The number of germ layers is a basis of animal classification.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Explain how birds are adapted for flight.
questions.answer: Birds have forelimbs modified into wings, feathers, a streamlined body and pneumatic bones with air cavities that reduce body weight.
questions.explanation: These features make the body light and suited for flying.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: Root hairs are found in the
questions.explanation: Root hairs arise in the zone of maturation and absorb water and minerals.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: The type of venation in the leaves of monocotyledons is generally
questions.explanation: Monocot leaves usually show parallel venation, whereas dicot leaves show reticulate venation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: The banyan tree supports its heavy branches with
questions.explanation: Prop roots grow down from the branches of the banyan and act as pillars.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: In angiosperm phloem, each sieve tube element is closely associated with a
questions.explanation: Companion cells regulate the functioning of sieve tube elements.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: Annual rings in the trunk of a tree growing in a temperate region form because
options: vascular cambium is more active in some seasons than others
phloem is produced only once a year
questions.explanation: Cambium produces large-lumen wood in spring and narrow-lumen wood in autumn, giving visible rings.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: Marginal placentation, with ovules along the ventral suture of a single-chambered ovary, is found in
questions.explanation: Pea and other legumes have a monocarpellary ovary with marginal placentation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: Differentiate between a tap root system and a fibrous root system with an example of each.
questions.answer: A tap root system has a main root developed from the radicle with lateral branches, as in mustard (dicots); a fibrous root system has many thin roots arising from the base of the stem, as in wheat (monocots).
keyPoints: Tap root from radicle, e.g. mustard
Fibrous roots from stem base, e.g. wheat
Taproot in dicots, fibrous in monocots
questions.explanation: In monocots the primary root is short lived and replaced by fibrous roots.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: Why do dicot stems show secondary growth while monocot stems usually do not?
questions.answer: Dicot stems have open vascular bundles with cambium between xylem and phloem, which divides to add secondary tissues; monocot bundles are closed and lack cambium.
keyPoints: Dicot bundles are open with cambium
Monocot bundles are closed without cambium
Cambium produces secondary xylem and phloem
questions.explanation: Presence of cambium makes secondary thickening possible.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The tissue that lines the cavities of the body and forms the covering of organs is
questions.explanation: Epithelial tissue forms the covering or lining of body surfaces and cavities.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Intercalated discs are a feature of
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle cells are joined by intercalated discs with gap junctions for rapid communication.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The abdomen of a cockroach is made up of how many segments?
questions.explanation: The cockroach abdomen has ten segments in both sexes.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The blood-like fluid that fills the body cavity of a cockroach is called
questions.explanation: Cockroach blood is haemolymph, which is colourless and lacks respiratory pigment.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: In the frog, mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood takes place mainly in the
questions.explanation: The frog has a three-chambered heart with a single ventricle, so blood mixes there.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Dense regular connective tissue that attaches a skeletal muscle to a bone is called a
questions.explanation: Tendons attach muscle to bone; ligaments attach bone to bone.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Name the three types of cell junctions found in animal tissues and state the function of each.
questions.answer: Tight junctions prevent leakage of substances across a tissue; adhering junctions cement neighbouring cells together; gap junctions connect the cytoplasm of adjoining cells to allow transfer of ions and small molecules.
questions.explanation: Junctions are found especially in epithelial and other tissues.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Why is the vision of a cockroach described as mosaic vision?
questions.answer: Each compound eye has about 2000 hexagonal ommatidia, and each forms a separate image part, so the image is a mosaic; it gives more sensitivity but less resolution.
keyPoints: Each ommatidium forms a part of the image
Gives mosaic image, more sensitivity but less resolution
questions.explanation: Vision with many ommatidia is called mosaic vision.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which cell organelle is called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce most of the cell's ATP through aerobic respiration.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane was proposed by
questions.explanation: Singer and Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model in 1972.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The ribosomes of prokaryotic cells have a sedimentation coefficient of
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S, made of 50S and 30S subunits.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The site of synthesis of ribosomal RNA and assembly of ribosome subunits in the nucleus is the
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is a non-membrane-bound region rich in rRNA and protein.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A drug stops the functioning of the Golgi apparatus in a gland cell. Which process would be affected most directly?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus modifies, packages and dispatches proteins and lipids for secretion.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which pair of organelles contains its own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria and chloroplasts are semi-autonomous organelles.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Write any three differences between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
questions.answer: Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles, have 70S ribosomes and a single circular DNA; eukaryotic cells have a true nucleus, membrane-bound organelles and 80S ribosomes.
questions.explanation: These are the main structural differences.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Pancreatic acinar cells that secrete digestive enzymes are rich in rough endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi bodies. Explain why.
questions.answer: Digestive enzymes are proteins made by ribosomes on the RER, which folds and transports them; the Golgi then modifies, packs and secretes them, so cells that secrete much protein need large amounts of both.
keyPoints: Heavy secretion needs more of both
questions.explanation: Organelle abundance matches the cell's function.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The monomers of proteins are
questions.explanation: Proteins are polymers of amino acids.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Two amino acids are joined together by a
questions.explanation: A peptide bond forms between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of the next.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Enzymes increase the rate of a reaction by
options: being used up in the reaction
questions.explanation: Enzymes lower the energy barrier and are not consumed.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Malonate inhibits succinic dehydrogenase because it
questions.explanation: Malonate is a competitive inhibitor that competes with succinate for the active site.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: An enzyme has a Vmax of 100 units. At a substrate concentration equal to its Km, the reaction velocity will be
questions.explanation: Km is the substrate concentration at which the velocity is half of Vmax.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Humans cannot digest cellulose even though it is a polymer of glucose, because they lack an enzyme that
questions.explanation: Cellulose has beta 1-4 linkages, unlike starch which has alpha linkages digestible by amylase.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Briefly describe the primary, secondary and tertiary structures of a protein.
questions.answer: Primary structure is the linear sequence of amino acids; secondary structure is the regular folding into alpha helix or beta pleated sheet; tertiary structure is the overall three-dimensional folding of the chain.
questions.explanation: A fourth level, quaternary, arises when several chains join.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Why can the effect of a competitive inhibitor be reduced by adding more substrate?
questions.answer: The inhibitor and substrate compete for the same active site; at a high substrate concentration the substrate outnumbers the inhibitor and occupies most active sites, so the inhibition is overcome.
keyPoints: Both bind the same active site
questions.explanation: This is the characteristic of competitive inhibition.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: DNA replication takes place in the
questions.explanation: DNA is duplicated during the S (synthesis) phase of interphase.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Synapsis, the pairing of homologous chromosomes, occurs during
questions.explanation: In zygotene of prophase I, homologous chromosomes pair to form bivalents.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Crossing over takes place during which sub-stage of meiotic prophase I?
questions.explanation: Recombination nodules appear and crossing over occurs in pachytene.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A cell with 20 chromosomes (2n = 20) undergoes meiosis. How many chromosomes does each cell have at the end of meiosis I?
questions.explanation: Meiosis I is reductional, so each daughter cell has n = 10 chromosomes.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A plant cell has 2n = 14. How many chromatids are present at metaphase of mitosis?
questions.explanation: At metaphase there are 14 chromosomes, each with two chromatids, giving 28.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which event in meiosis most directly increases genetic variation?
options: Exchange of segments between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes
Duplication of DNA in S phase
questions.explanation: Crossing over and independent assortment produce new gene combinations.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: What is cytokinesis? How does it differ in plant and animal cells?
questions.answer: Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm after karyokinesis. Animal cells form a cleavage furrow that pinches the cell, while plant cells form a cell plate in the centre that grows outward.
questions.explanation: The rigid wall of plant cells requires a cell plate.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Why is meiosis essential in sexually reproducing organisms?
questions.answer: It halves the chromosome number in gametes so that fertilisation restores the diploid number, keeping it constant across generations, and it creates variation through crossing over.
questions.explanation: Without meiosis the chromosome number would double every generation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The main pigment that takes part directly in the light reaction of photosynthesis is
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll a is the primary pigment; the others are accessory pigments.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The dark (biosynthetic) reaction of photosynthesis takes place in the
questions.explanation: The Calvin cycle occurs in the stroma of the chloroplast.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The first stable product of CO2 fixation in C3 plants is
questions.explanation: RuBisCO fixes CO2 to RuBP to form two molecules of 3-PGA.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The most abundant enzyme on Earth, which catalyses both carboxylation and oxygenation, is
questions.explanation: RuBisCO acts as a carboxylase in the Calvin cycle and as an oxygenase in photorespiration.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: In C4 plants the primary fixation of CO2 in mesophyll cells is catalysed by
questions.explanation: PEP carboxylase fixes CO2 to PEP forming oxaloacetic acid, a four-carbon compound.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Photorespiration is negligible in C4 plants because
options: CO2 is concentrated around RuBisCO in bundle sheath cells
questions.explanation: Concentrated CO2 prevents RuBisCO from acting as an oxygenase.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: What are the products of the light reaction and where does the oxygen come from?
questions.answer: The light reaction yields ATP and NADPH; the oxygen released comes from the splitting (photolysis) of water, not from CO2.
questions.explanation: Water splitting is associated with photosystem II.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Compare cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation.
questions.answer: Non-cyclic involves both PS II and PS I, gives ATP, NADPH and O2; cyclic involves only PS I, electrons return to it, and only ATP is made, with no NADPH or oxygen.
keyPoints: Non-cyclic: PS I and PS II, ATP + NADPH + O2
Cyclic: PS I only, ATP only
questions.explanation: Cyclic flow occurs in the stroma lamellae.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Glycolysis takes place in the
questions.explanation: Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm of all living cells.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The end product of glycolysis is
questions.explanation: One glucose molecule is broken down into two molecules of pyruvic acid.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The net gain of ATP molecules from glycolysis of one glucose molecule is
questions.explanation: Four ATP are produced and two are consumed, giving a net gain of two.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The final acceptor of electrons in the mitochondrial electron transport chain is
questions.explanation: Cytochrome c oxidase passes electrons to oxygen, forming water.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The respiratory quotient (RQ) when fats are the respiratory substrate is generally
questions.explanation: Fats contain less oxygen than carbohydrates, so more oxygen is consumed than CO2 released; for tripalmitin RQ is about 0.7.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: When yeast ferments glucose in the absence of oxygen, pyruvic acid is converted into
questions.explanation: Alcoholic fermentation yields ethanol and CO2.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Differentiate between aerobic and anaerobic respiration.
questions.answer: Aerobic respiration needs oxygen and completely oxidises glucose to CO2 and water, releasing much energy; anaerobic respiration occurs without oxygen, gives incomplete oxidation (alcohol or lactic acid) and releases little energy.
questions.explanation: Fermentation is the anaerobic route in yeast.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Why is the energy yield of fermentation much lower than that of aerobic respiration?
questions.answer: In fermentation glucose is only partially broken down and the electron transport chain is not used, so only 2 ATP are made by glycolysis, while aerobic respiration oxidises pyruvate fully and gains many more ATP through oxidative phosphorylation.
questions.explanation: Most ATP comes from the electron transport chain.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The plant hormone that promotes apical dominance and cell elongation is
questions.explanation: Auxins such as IAA are produced at the shoot tip and cause cell elongation and apical dominance.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The gaseous hormone that promotes fruit ripening is
questions.explanation: Ethylene hastens ripening of fruits such as tomato and banana.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Bolting, the sudden elongation of the internodes in rosette plants like cabbage, is caused by
questions.explanation: Gibberellins promote internode elongation and bolting before flowering.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which hormone promotes cell division and delays senescence of leaves?
questions.explanation: Cytokinins, first isolated as kinetin, stimulate cytokinesis and delay leaf ageing.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: During a drought, closure of stomata to reduce water loss is mainly brought about by
questions.explanation: ABA is the stress hormone that causes stomatal closure.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Winter varieties of wheat flower in the following summer only after exposure to cold. This process is called
questions.explanation: Vernalisation is the promotion of flowering by exposure to low temperature.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Name the three phases of growth in a plant cell and state what happens in each.
questions.answer: Meristematic phase: cells divide actively. Elongation phase: cells enlarge with vacuolation and new wall deposition. Maturation phase: cells attain their final size and structure and differentiate.
questions.explanation: These phases are seen in root and shoot apices.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Explain how removing the shoot tip of a plant makes it grow more side branches.
questions.answer: The shoot tip makes auxin that moves down and inhibits growth of axillary buds (apical dominance). Removing the tip removes this auxin, so the lateral buds grow into branches.
questions.explanation: Gardeners prune hedges to make them bushy for this reason.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The enzyme present in saliva that starts digestion of starch is
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase breaks starch into maltose in the buccal cavity.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Most of the absorption of digested food takes place in the
questions.explanation: The small intestine, with villi, is the main site of absorption.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Bile, which helps in the emulsification of fats, is produced by the
questions.explanation: Bile is made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The major portion of carbon dioxide in blood is transported as
questions.explanation: About 70 per cent of CO2 is carried as bicarbonate in the plasma.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which is the correct order of conduction of the cardiac impulse?
options: SA node, AV node, bundle of His, Purkinje fibres
AV node, SA node, bundle of His, Purkinje fibres
SA node, Purkinje fibres, bundle of His, AV node
Bundle of His, SA node, AV node, Purkinje fibres
questions.explanation: The SA node is the pacemaker; the impulse passes to the AV node, the bundle of His and then Purkinje fibres.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A person has a tidal volume of 500 mL, inspiratory reserve volume of 3000 mL and expiratory reserve volume of 1100 mL. The vital capacity is
questions.explanation: Vital capacity = TV + IRV + ERV = 500 + 3000 + 1100 = 4600 mL.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: State the role of HCl and pepsinogen in the stomach.
questions.answer: HCl provides an acidic medium (pH about 1.8), kills microbes and converts inactive pepsinogen into active pepsin; pepsin then breaks proteins into proteoses and peptones.
keyPoints: HCl gives acid pH and kills germs
questions.explanation: Gastric glands secrete both, and mucus protects the stomach wall.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Explain why haemoglobin releases more oxygen in actively respiring tissues.
questions.answer: Tissues have a high pCO2, high H+ concentration (low pH) and higher temperature, and these lower the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen, shifting the dissociation curve to the right so more oxygen is released.
keyPoints: High pCO2 and H+, lower pH, higher temperature
Reduced affinity of haemoglobin for O2
Curve shifts to right, more O2 released
questions.explanation: This is the Bohr effect.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The functional unit of the kidney is the
questions.explanation: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The hormone that increases water reabsorption in the distal parts of the nephron is
questions.explanation: ADH released from the neurohypophysis prevents loss of water in urine.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The sodium-potassium pump of a neuron maintains the resting potential by moving
questions.explanation: The pump moves three sodium ions out and two potassium ions in per cycle.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: During muscle contraction, calcium ions bind to
questions.explanation: Ca2+ binds troponin, exposing myosin-binding sites on actin.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A person feels constant thirst, passes a large volume of urine and has glucose in the urine, because of too little insulin action. The condition is
questions.explanation: Lack of insulin raises blood glucose; excess glucose spills into urine (glycosuria).

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: In a healthy adult the glomerular filtration rate is about
questions.explanation: GFR is about 125 mL per minute, i.e. about 180 litres a day.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Describe the path of a reflex arc.
questions.answer: A stimulus excites a receptor; the sensory (afferent) neuron carries the impulse to the spinal cord, where it is passed to a motor (efferent) neuron, often via an interneuron, which takes it to the effector, producing the response.
questions.explanation: A reflex is an involuntary rapid response.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Explain how the renin-angiotensin mechanism raises blood pressure when the glomerular filtration falls.
questions.answer: A fall in GFR makes the juxtaglomerular cells release renin, which leads to formation of angiotensin II; this narrows blood vessels and stimulates the adrenal cortex to release aldosterone, causing Na+ and water reabsorption, which restores blood volume and pressure.
keyPoints: Aldosterone increases Na+ and water reabsorption
questions.explanation: This restores GFR.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: The science of identifying, naming and classifying organisms is called
questions.explanation: Taxonomy deals with the characterisation, identification, nomenclature and classification of organisms.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: A store house of dried, pressed and preserved plant specimens mounted on sheets is called a
questions.explanation: A herbarium preserves plant specimens for study and reference.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: Which kingdom contains heterotrophic organisms whose cell walls are made of chitin?
questions.explanation: Fungi are heterotrophs with cell walls of chitin and other polysaccharides.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: The lion (Panthera leo) and the tiger (Panthera tigris) belong to the same
questions.explanation: They share the genus Panthera but are different species.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: A taxonomic key is arranged as a series of pairs of contrasting characters. Each such pair is called a
questions.explanation: In a key each pair of contrasting statements is a couplet, and each statement is a lead.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: Potato (Solanum tuberosum) and brinjal (Solanum melongena) are placed in the same
options: genus and family but different species
questions.explanation: Both belong to genus Solanum (and family Solanaceae) but have different species names.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: Distinguish between a botanical garden and a herbarium.
questions.answer: A botanical garden has living plants grown and labelled for study and display; a herbarium holds dried, pressed and preserved plant specimens on sheets.
questions.explanation: Both are taxonomical aids.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: Why are scientific names preferred to local names for identifying organisms worldwide?
questions.answer: One organism can have many local names in different regions, and one name may refer to different organisms, causing confusion; a scientific name is unique, universally accepted and follows fixed rules.
keyPoints: Local names vary and cause confusion
Scientific name is unique for each species
questions.explanation: Universal naming is the purpose of nomenclature.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The unicellular alga often used as a food supplement by space travellers is
questions.explanation: Chlorella is rich in protein and is used as single-cell protein.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Agar, used to grow microbes, is obtained from
questions.explanation: Gelidium and Gracilaria, which are red algae, yield agar.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The coralloid roots of Cycas are associated with
questions.explanation: Coralloid roots contain N2-fixing cyanobacteria such as Anabaena.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The endosperm formed after double fertilisation in angiosperms is
questions.explanation: Triple fusion of one male gamete with two polar nuclei gives triploid endosperm.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which of the following plants is heterosporous?
questions.explanation: Selaginella produces two kinds of spores, microspores and megaspores.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: In a moss, the spore germinates to form a green, creeping, branched stage called the
questions.explanation: The protonema is the first stage of the haploid gametophyte of mosses.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: State two differences between gymnosperms and angiosperms.
questions.answer: Gymnosperms have naked ovules and seeds, no flowers or fruits and no true vessels in the xylem; angiosperms have ovules enclosed in an ovary, bear flowers, form fruits and have vessels.
keyPoints: Flowers and fruits absent or present
Vessels absent or present in xylem
questions.explanation: Angiosperms are the most advanced seed plants.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: What is alternation of generations? Explain with reference to a fern.
questions.answer: It is the alternation of a diploid sporophytic phase and a haploid gametophytic phase in the life cycle. In a fern the diploid sporophyte bears spores that give a haploid prothallus, which bears gametes whose fusion gives the sporophyte again.
keyPoints: Prothallus makes gametes, zygote gives sporophyte
questions.explanation: Ferns show a diplohaplontic life cycle.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The presence of a notochord at some stage of life is a feature of phylum
questions.explanation: Notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord and pharyngeal gill slits characterise chordates.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which of the following has a cartilaginous endoskeleton?
questions.explanation: Scoliodon (dogfish) belongs to Chondrichthyes, the cartilaginous fishes.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Metamerism, the division of the body into similar segments, is seen in phylum
questions.explanation: Earthworms and leeches show metameric segmentation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which feature is found only in class Mammalia?
questions.explanation: Mammary glands for suckling the young are unique to mammals; birds also have four-chambered hearts.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: An animal has a chitinous exoskeleton, jointed legs, a body divided into head, thorax and abdomen, and sheds its exoskeleton periodically. It belongs to
questions.explanation: Arthropods, such as insects, have a chitinous cuticle that is moulted.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A soft-bodied animal with a calcareous shell, a muscular foot, a mantle and a rasping organ called the radula belongs to
questions.explanation: Radula, mantle and muscular foot are features of Mollusca, e.g. snail and Pila.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Write two differences between cartilaginous fishes and bony fishes.
questions.answer: Cartilaginous fishes (Chondrichthyes) have a cartilage endoskeleton, placoid scales, no air bladder and gill slits without an operculum; bony fishes (Osteichthyes) have a bony skeleton, cycloid or ctenoid scales, an air bladder and an operculum covering the gills.
keyPoints: Operculum and air bladder absent or present
questions.explanation: These are the two classes of fishes.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Why is class Amphibia so named? Mention two features of an amphibian.
questions.answer: Amphibians can live both in water and on land. They have moist skin without scales, a three-chambered heart, and respire through gills, lungs and skin.
keyPoints: Live in water and on land
questions.explanation: The name comes from the Greek for 'double life'.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: The male reproductive whorl of a flower is called the
questions.explanation: The androecium consists of stamens, each with an anther and a filament.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: The mango fruit is an example of a
questions.explanation: A mango has a fleshy mesocarp and a hard stony endocarp, so it is a drupe.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: In dicot leaves the guard cells of stomata are
questions.explanation: Guard cells are bean (kidney) shaped in dicots and dumb-bell shaped in grasses.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: Living cells with thickened corners due to deposition of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin that give mechanical support form
questions.explanation: Collenchyma is a living supporting tissue, found below the epidermis of dicot stems.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: A transverse section of a stem shows scattered vascular bundles, each closed and surrounded by a sclerenchymatous sheath. The stem belongs to
questions.explanation: Scattered, closed bundles with a sclerenchymatous sheath are typical of monocot stems such as maize.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: In a flower the ovary is placed above the other floral parts, which arise from below it. This condition is
questions.explanation: Hypogynous flowers (mustard, brinjal) have a superior ovary.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: Distinguish between the anatomy of a dorsiventral (dicot) leaf and an isobilateral (monocot) leaf.
questions.answer: A dicot leaf has differentiated palisade and spongy mesophyll and more stomata on the lower surface; a monocot leaf has undifferentiated mesophyll, similar stomata on both surfaces and bulliform cells in the upper epidermis.
keyPoints: Stomata mostly lower or on both surfaces
questions.explanation: These differences are seen in transverse sections.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: Why is the heartwood of an old tree dark in colour and unable to conduct water?
questions.answer: In heartwood the xylem elements are filled with tannins, resins, gums and oils and their lumens are blocked by tyloses. It is hard, durable and resistant to microbes, and provides mechanical support but no water conduction.
questions.explanation: Sapwood, the outer region, conducts water.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The tissue that stores fat in the body is
questions.explanation: Adipose tissue is a loose connective tissue rich in fat-storing cells.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which blood cells help in the clotting of blood?
questions.explanation: Platelets (thrombocytes) release substances that trigger clotting.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A frog can absorb oxygen directly through its moist
questions.explanation: Cutaneous respiration through the skin is used in water and during hibernation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The excretory organs of a cockroach are
questions.explanation: Malpighian tubules at the junction of the midgut and hindgut remove nitrogenous waste.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: In a male frog, the duct that carries both sperms and urine to the cloaca is the
questions.explanation: The ureter acts as a urinogenital duct in the male frog.

crossCheck.note: In male frog the sperm and urine share the urinogenital duct, which is the ureter in males; 'urethra' is not the standard term here, so the key option is best guess but the wording is loose. Reviewed: kept; matches NCERT.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The walls of the lung alveoli and blood capillaries are lined with simple squamous epithelium mainly because the thin flat cells
options: help in diffusion of gases and other substances
questions.explanation: A thin one-cell layer favours rapid diffusion and filtration.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Write three differences between skeletal muscle and smooth muscle.
questions.answer: Skeletal muscle is striated, multinucleate and voluntary, attached to bones; smooth muscle is non-striated, uninucleate, spindle shaped and involuntary, found in walls of hollow organs.
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle is striated but involuntary.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A cockroach has no respiratory pigment in its blood, yet its cells get enough oxygen. Explain.
questions.answer: Air enters through spiracles into a network of tracheae and tracheoles that carry oxygen directly to the tissues, so the haemolymph does not need to transport oxygen.
questions.explanation: Insect respiration is by a tracheal system.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The term 'cell' was first used by
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke observed cork cells in 1665 and called them cells.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The statement that new cells arise from pre-existing cells was made by
questions.explanation: Virchow stated 'omnis cellula-e cellula', modifying the cell theory.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The main component of the plant cell wall is
questions.explanation: Plant cell walls are made mainly of cellulose, hemicellulose and pectins.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which organelles, containing hydrolytic enzymes, are called 'suicide bags'?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes may burst and digest the cell if their enzymes leak out.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which of the following cell components is NOT bounded by a membrane?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are made of RNA and protein and have no limiting membrane.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The inner membrane of a mitochondrion is folded into cristae. This increases
options: the surface area for the enzymes of oxidative phosphorylation
questions.explanation: More inner membrane carries more electron transport components and ATP synthase.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Distinguish between passive transport and active transport across the cell membrane.
questions.answer: Passive transport moves substances down the concentration gradient without using energy, as in diffusion; active transport moves substances against the gradient using ATP, as in the sodium-potassium pump.
questions.explanation: Carrier proteins are involved in active transport.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A plant cell and an animal cell are placed in pure water. Predict and explain what happens to each.
questions.answer: Water enters both by osmosis. The plant cell becomes turgid but does not burst because the rigid cell wall resists expansion; the animal cell has no wall, so it swells and may burst.
questions.explanation: Pure water is hypotonic to the cell contents.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The most abundant protein in the animal world is
questions.explanation: Collagen is the most abundant protein in animals, while RuBisCO is the most abundant in the biosphere.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The reserve carbohydrate in animals is
questions.explanation: Glycogen is stored mainly in the liver and muscles.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Enzymes that catalyse the joining of two compounds, using energy from ATP, belong to the class
questions.explanation: Ligases join substrates, usually with ATP hydrolysis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A nucleoside consists of
options: a nitrogenous base and a phosphate group
a sugar and a phosphate group
a nitrogenous base and a pentose sugar
questions.explanation: Adding a phosphate group to a nucleoside gives a nucleotide.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Zinc is a cofactor required for the activity of the enzyme
questions.explanation: Carboxypeptidase needs Zn2+ as a cofactor.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A sample of double-stranded DNA contains 30 per cent adenine. What percentage of guanine does it contain?
questions.explanation: A = T = 30 per cent, so G + C = 40 per cent, i.e. G = 20 per cent.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: What is a prosthetic group? Give one example.
questions.answer: A prosthetic group is an organic non-protein part tightly bound to the apoenzyme, needed for activity. Example: haem in the enzymes peroxidase and catalase.
keyPoints: Tightly bound to the enzyme protein
Example: haem in peroxidase or catalase
questions.explanation: Prosthetic groups, coenzymes and metal ions are all cofactors.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Explain how changes in pH affect the activity of an enzyme.
questions.answer: Each enzyme works best at an optimum pH. Away from it, the charges on the amino acids of the active site change, altering the shape of the protein, so substrate binding falls and activity decreases.
keyPoints: Extreme pH changes charge and shape
questions.explanation: For example pepsin works at acid pH and trypsin at alkaline pH.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The inactive stage in which cells exit the cell cycle and no longer divide is called
questions.explanation: Cells in G0 remain metabolically active but do not proliferate.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Chromosomes line up at the equatorial plate during
questions.explanation: In metaphase chromosomes are aligned at the equator with spindle fibres attached to their kinetochores.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: In a typical human cell that divides once in about 24 hours, the duration of mitosis (M phase) is only about
questions.explanation: Mitosis is short, about an hour; most of the cycle is spent in interphase.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The nuclear envelope reappears and chromosomes decondense during
questions.explanation: Telophase is the reverse of prophase in these events.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which of the following distinguishes anaphase I of meiosis from anaphase of mitosis?
options: Homologous chromosomes, not sister chromatids, separate
questions.explanation: In anaphase I whole homologous chromosomes move to opposite poles; the centromeres do not split.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A somatic cell with 8 chromosomes divides by mitosis. Each daughter cell will have
questions.explanation: Mitosis is equational, so the chromosome number is the same as in the parent cell.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Describe the main events of prophase of mitosis.
questions.answer: Chromatin condenses into chromosomes made of two chromatids; the centrioles move to opposite poles and the spindle starts to form; the nucleolus and nuclear envelope begin to disappear.
questions.explanation: Prophase follows the G2 phase.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Compare anaphase I and anaphase II of meiosis.
questions.answer: In anaphase I homologous chromosomes, each with two chromatids, separate and go to opposite poles; in anaphase II the centromeres divide and sister chromatids separate, as in mitosis.
keyPoints: Centromere divides only in anaphase II
questions.explanation: Reduction in chromosome number takes place in meiosis I.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Joseph Priestley's experiments with a mint plant and a candle showed that plants
options: restore to the air whatever burning candles remove
questions.explanation: Priestley concluded plants restore the air, later shown to be oxygen.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The final hydrogen acceptor of the light reaction of photosynthesis is
questions.explanation: NADP+ is reduced to NADPH in the light reaction.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The reaction centre chlorophyll a of photosystem I absorbs light best at a wavelength of
questions.explanation: PS I has P700, and PS II has P680.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: For fixing each molecule of CO2, the Calvin cycle requires
questions.explanation: Three ATP and two NADPH are used per CO2 fixed.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: How many turns of the Calvin cycle are required to synthesise one molecule of glucose?
questions.explanation: One CO2 is fixed per turn and glucose has six carbons.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The rate of photosynthesis does not increase when light intensity is raised, because CO2 concentration is very low. This illustrates
questions.explanation: Blackman's law says the factor in shortest supply limits the rate.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Explain the chemiosmotic hypothesis of ATP synthesis in chloroplasts.
questions.answer: Photolysis of water and electron transport pump protons into the thylakoid lumen, building a proton gradient across the membrane. Protons flow back to the stroma through ATP synthase, which uses the energy to make ATP from ADP and Pi.
keyPoints: Proton gradient built in thylakoid lumen
ATP made from ADP and Pi
questions.explanation: The same principle operates in mitochondria.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: What is photorespiration and why is it considered wasteful?
questions.answer: In photorespiration RuBisCO binds O2 instead of CO2 in the presence of high oxygen and low CO2, so RuBP is oxidised and CO2 is released. It produces neither ATP nor NADPH and reduces sugar synthesis.
keyPoints: No ATP or NADPH made, reduces yield
questions.explanation: C3 plants lose a part of fixed carbon this way.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The Krebs cycle takes place in the
questions.explanation: The enzymes of the TCA cycle are located in the mitochondrial matrix.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The Krebs cycle starts with the condensation of acetyl CoA with
questions.explanation: Acetyl CoA joins oxaloacetic acid to form citric acid.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Oxidative phosphorylation, the synthesis of ATP in respiration, occurs by the enzyme ATP synthase located in the
questions.explanation: ATP synthase (complex V) is in the inner mitochondrial membrane.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: In one turn of the Krebs cycle, the number of NADH molecules formed is
questions.explanation: One turn gives 3 NADH, 1 FADH2 and 1 GTP (or ATP), and releases 2 CO2.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: How many CO2 molecules are released when one glucose molecule is completely oxidised, starting from glycolysis through the Krebs cycle?
questions.explanation: Each pyruvate gives 3 CO2 (1 in the link reaction, 2 in the cycle), so two pyruvate give 6.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Complete oxidation of tripalmitin uses 72.5 molecules of O2 and releases 51 molecules of CO2. Its respiratory quotient is about

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: What is the role of oxygen in aerobic respiration?
questions.answer: Oxygen acts as the final acceptor of electrons and protons in the electron transport chain, forming water; this lets NADH and FADH2 be reoxidised so that ATP production can continue.
keyPoints: Keeps electron transport and ATP synthesis going
questions.explanation: Without oxygen the electron transport chain stops.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Why is the respiratory pathway described as amphibolic?
questions.answer: It involves both breakdown (catabolism) of carbohydrates, fats and proteins to release energy, and the supply of intermediates such as acetyl CoA and organic acids that are used to synthesise fatty acids and amino acids.
questions.explanation: Amphibolic pathways serve both catabolic and anabolic functions.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The growth movement of a plant part towards light is called
questions.explanation: Shoots bend towards light, showing positive phototropism.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The process by which cells derived from meristems become specialised for specific functions is
questions.explanation: Differentiation produces structurally and functionally distinct cell types.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The response of flowering to the relative duration of day and night is called
questions.explanation: Photoperiodism classifies plants as short-day, long-day or day-neutral.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: In the sigmoid growth curve, the phase in which growth is fastest is the
questions.explanation: In the log phase the growth rate increases rapidly.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which combination correctly describes the role of two hormones in seed dormancy?
options: Gibberellin induces dormancy and ABA breaks it
ABA induces dormancy and gibberellin breaks it
Ethylene breaks dormancy and auxin induces it
questions.explanation: ABA maintains dormancy; gibberellins promote germination.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Seedless fruits can be produced without fertilisation, a process called parthenocarpy, by spraying flowers with
questions.explanation: Auxins and gibberellins can induce parthenocarpy, e.g. in tomatoes.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Distinguish between differentiation, dedifferentiation and redifferentiation.
questions.answer: Differentiation: cells from meristems become specialised. Dedifferentiation: living differentiated cells regain the capacity to divide, as in cambium formation. Redifferentiation: such cells lose the ability to divide again and mature for specific functions.
keyPoints: Redifferentiation: mature again for a function
questions.explanation: Interfascicular cambium arises by dedifferentiation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Ethephon, a compound that releases ethylene, is widely used in agriculture. Give three uses and explain the reasoning.
questions.answer: Ethylene hastens fruit ripening (tomato, apple), promotes flowering in pineapple so that fruits form together, and promotes female flowers in cucumbers, increasing yield; it also causes abscission of leaves and fruits.
questions.explanation: Ethylene is a gaseous plant hormone.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The largest gland in the human body is the
questions.explanation: The liver weighs about 1.2 to 1.5 kg in an adult.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The muscular partition separating the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity is the
questions.explanation: Contraction of the diaphragm increases the thoracic volume in inspiration.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The total number of permanent teeth in an adult human is
questions.explanation: The dental formula 2123/2123 gives 32 teeth.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The average lifespan of a human red blood cell is about
questions.explanation: RBCs live about 120 days and are destroyed in the spleen.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A person with blood group AB is a universal recipient because the plasma of this group
options: has both anti-A and anti-B antibodies
has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies
questions.explanation: Group AB has A and B antigens on RBCs and no anti-A or anti-B antibodies in plasma.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Erythroblastosis foetalis can occur when
options: an Rh positive mother carries an Rh negative foetus
an Rh negative mother carries an Rh positive foetus
both parents have blood group O
questions.explanation: Rh antibodies of an Rh-negative mother can cross the placenta and attack the red cells of an Rh-positive foetus in a later pregnancy.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Calculate the cardiac output of a person whose stroke volume is 70 mL and heart rate is 72 beats per minute.
questions.answer: Cardiac output = stroke volume x heart rate = 70 mL x 72 = 5040 mL per minute, about 5 litres per minute.
keyPoints: Cardiac output = stroke volume x heart rate
questions.explanation: The average human cardiac output is about 5 litres per minute.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Explain which features make the alveoli efficient sites for exchange of gases.
questions.answer: The alveoli have very thin walls of squamous epithelium, a very large combined surface area, and a rich network of capillaries, so oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse rapidly across a short distance.
questions.explanation: Each lung has millions of alveoli.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The main nitrogenous waste excreted by humans is
questions.explanation: Humans are ureotelic; urea is formed in the liver.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The number of bones in the adult human skeleton is
questions.explanation: The adult human skeleton has 206 bones.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The joint at the shoulder is an example of a
questions.explanation: The shoulder and hip are ball and socket joints, allowing movement in many directions.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The gland called the master gland because it controls other endocrine glands is the
questions.explanation: The pituitary secretes tropic hormones that control other glands.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Enlargement of the thyroid gland, called simple goitre, is caused by
options: deficiency of iodine in the diet
questions.explanation: Lack of iodine reduces thyroid hormone production and the gland enlarges.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Nerve impulses travel faster in myelinated nerve fibres because the impulse
options: jumps from one node of Ranvier to the next
questions.explanation: Myelin insulates the axon, so depolarisation occurs only at the nodes (saltatory conduction).

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which hormones regulate blood calcium levels? State the action of each.
questions.answer: Parathyroid hormone raises blood Ca2+ by increasing its release from bone and reabsorption in kidneys; calcitonin from the thyroid lowers blood Ca2+ by reducing bone resorption.
questions.explanation: The two hormones act in opposite ways.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Why does a nerve impulse pass across a chemical synapse in only one direction?
questions.answer: Neurotransmitter vesicles are present only in the axon terminal of the pre-synaptic neuron and receptors only on the post-synaptic membrane, so the transmitter can act only in one direction.
keyPoints: Neurotransmitter stored in the pre-synaptic terminal
questions.explanation: This ensures orderly transmission of information.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: Which is the highest (largest) category in the taxonomic hierarchy?
questions.explanation: Kingdom is the broadest category and includes several phyla.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: A group of related genera is placed in a
questions.explanation: Related genera form a family, and related families form an order.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: Growth in living organisms differs from that in non-living objects because living things grow
options: from inside, by cell division or cell enlargement
by sticking material on the outside
only in size, never in number of cells
only in the presence of light
questions.explanation: Non-living objects such as a mountain or a sand mound grow by accumulation of material on the surface.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: The sum total of all the chemical reactions occurring in the body of a living organism is called
questions.explanation: Metabolism is a defining feature of all living organisms.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: Why is reproduction NOT accepted as a defining feature that applies to every living organism?
options: Some living organisms, such as mules and worker bees, do not reproduce
questions.explanation: Mules and worker bees are alive but sterile, so reproduction cannot define all living things.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: A student isolates metabolic enzymes from cells and carries out the reactions in a test tube. These reactions are
options: living reactions, but the test tube contents are not a living organism
non-living reactions that do not need enzymes
proof that the test tube is alive
questions.explanation: Isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are living reactions, but not a living organism.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: How does the growth of a living organism differ from the growth of a non-living object? Give an example of each.
questions.answer: Living organisms grow from inside by cell division and enlargement, e.g. a seedling; non-living objects grow only by accumulation of material on the outside, e.g. a mountain or a sand pile.
questions.explanation: Growth in living things is intrinsic.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: The Living World and Biological Classification
questions.q: Why do classification systems of organisms keep changing as new information is gathered?
questions.answer: Classification is based on characters such as cell structure, body organisation, reproduction and evolutionary relationships. As new characters are found through better tools and studies, groups are re-arranged to show natural relationships better.
keyPoints: Groups are revised to show relationships
questions.explanation: Whittaker's five kingdoms replaced the earlier two-kingdom system for this reason.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which group of algae has chlorophyll a and b and stores starch, like higher plants?
questions.explanation: Green algae (Chlorophyceae) have chlorophyll a and b and store starch.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Floridean starch is the stored food of
questions.explanation: Red algae (Rhodophyceae) store floridean starch.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Peat, used as fuel and as packing material for living plants, is obtained from
questions.explanation: Sphagnum, a moss, accumulates as peat and holds much water.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A typical mature embryo sac of an angiosperm contains how many cells?
questions.explanation: The embryo sac is seven-celled and eight-nucleate.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Gymnosperms do not depend on water for fertilisation, because
options: their male gametes are flagellated and swim in air
the pollen tube carries non-motile male gametes to the egg
they are fertilised by the sporophyte
questions.explanation: Pollen tubes deliver the male gametes directly to the egg in seed plants.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A plant has a dominant, multicellular diploid sporophyte, while its gametophyte is reduced to a few cells. Its life cycle is
questions.explanation: In a diplontic cycle the diploid phase dominates, as in gymnosperms and angiosperms.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Mention three ways in which algae are useful to humans.
questions.answer: Algae carry out about half of the photosynthesis on earth and add oxygen; some, like Porphyra and Laminaria, are food; agar and algin come from red and brown algae; Chlorella is a protein supplement.
keyPoints: Source of agar, algin or single-cell protein
questions.explanation: Algae are also primary producers in water.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: How does the seed habit help plants to survive better than spore-producing plants?
questions.answer: A seed protects the embryo with a seed coat, contains stored food for the young plant, and has a dormant state that helps it survive unfavourable conditions and be dispersed; it also frees fertilisation from the need for water.
questions.explanation: The seed habit is a major evolutionary advance.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The numerous small pores on the body wall of a sponge are called
questions.explanation: Water enters through ostia and leaves through the osculum.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Fishes breathe through
questions.explanation: Fishes have gills for respiration in water.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which flatworm has hooks and suckers for attaching to the host's intestine?
questions.explanation: The tapeworm Taenia has a scolex with hooks and suckers.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The roundworms, which have a pseudocoelom, belong to phylum
questions.explanation: Aschelminthes (roundworms), e.g. Ascaris, are pseudocoelomates with separate sexes.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A bat flies but is classified as a mammal rather than a bird because it
options: has mammary glands, hair and gives birth to young
questions.explanation: Mammary glands, hair and viviparity are mammalian features; flight is not a deciding character.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Marine animals with eight rows of ciliated comb plates for locomotion and the ability to show bioluminescence belong to
questions.explanation: Ctenophores, or comb jellies, move with comb plates.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: List any three characteristics of phylum Arthropoda.
questions.answer: Arthropods have a chitinous exoskeleton, jointed appendages and a segmented body with an open circulatory system; they are bilaterally symmetrical and have a haemocoel.
questions.explanation: Arthropoda is the largest phylum.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Birds and mammals are called homeotherms. What does this mean and how does it help them?
questions.answer: They keep a constant body temperature irrespective of the surroundings; this lets them stay active and live in a wide range of habitats, hot or cold.
keyPoints: Allows a wide range of habitats
questions.explanation: Other vertebrates are poikilotherms.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: The embryonic part of a seed that grows into the root is the
questions.explanation: The radicle forms the primary root, and the plumule forms the shoot.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: The potato is a modified
questions.explanation: The potato tuber is a swollen underground stem with buds (eyes).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: The corolla of a pea flower is described as
questions.explanation: Pea has five petals: a standard, two wings and two keel petals, forming a papilionaceous corolla.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: The only living component of xylem is
questions.explanation: Tracheids, vessels and fibres are dead at maturity; xylem parenchyma is living.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: In the periderm of a woody stem, the phelloderm (secondary cortex) is formed
options: on the inner side of the cork cambium
questions.explanation: Phellogen cuts off phellem outwards and phelloderm inwards.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: In a dicot root, the xylem is described as exarch, which means that
options: xylem and phloem are in the same bundle
protoxylem lies towards the periphery and metaxylem towards the centre
questions.explanation: In roots, protoxylem is outer and metaxylem is inner (exarch condition).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: Differentiate between a simple leaf and a compound leaf with one example of each.
questions.answer: In a simple leaf the lamina is entire or incised but not cut to the midrib, as in mango; in a compound leaf the incisions reach the midrib or petiole, breaking the lamina into leaflets, as in neem.
questions.explanation: A bud is present in the axil of a leaf but not of a leaflet.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Morphology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
questions.q: What are bulliform cells? How do they help a grass leaf survive water shortage?
questions.answer: Bulliform cells are large, empty, colourless cells in the upper epidermis of grass leaves. When they lose water the leaf curls inward, reducing the surface exposed and so lowering water loss.
keyPoints: Large colourless cells in the upper epidermis
Flaccid cells make the leaf roll
questions.explanation: They are a feature of the isobilateral monocot leaf.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The mature bone cells are called
questions.explanation: Osteocytes lie in lacunae in the hard bone matrix.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Cartilage cells are called
questions.explanation: Chondrocytes lie in small cavities in the solid but pliable cartilage matrix.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: How many pairs of walking legs does a cockroach have?
questions.explanation: Each thoracic segment bears a pair of legs, so a cockroach has three pairs.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The mouth parts of a cockroach are of the
questions.explanation: Cockroach mouthparts include labrum, mandibles, maxillae and labium for chewing.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The epithelium that lines the ducts of glands and the tubular parts of nephrons, and helps in secretion and absorption, is
questions.explanation: Cuboidal epithelium has cube-shaped cells and is found in ducts of glands and nephron tubules.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The fertilised eggs of a cockroach are enclosed in a capsule called the
questions.explanation: A female cockroach produces ootheca, each containing about 14 to 16 eggs.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Distinguish between a tendon and a ligament.
questions.answer: A tendon is dense regular connective tissue connecting skeletal muscle to bone; a ligament is dense regular connective tissue connecting one bone to another bone.
keyPoints: Both are dense regular connective tissue
questions.explanation: Both are made of collagen fibres arranged in parallel rows.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: How do intercalated discs help the heart to work as a unit?
questions.answer: Intercalated discs join neighbouring cardiac muscle cells and contain gap junctions that let the impulse pass quickly from cell to cell, so that all the cells contract almost together.
keyPoints: Gap junctions allow quick spread of impulse
questions.explanation: This ensures coordinated beating.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The cell organelle where proteins are synthesised is the
questions.explanation: Ribosomes translate mRNA into proteins.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The membrane that bounds the vacuole in a plant cell is called the
questions.explanation: The tonoplast is the single membrane around the vacuole.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Each centriole has a cartwheel-like structure made of
options: nine doublet microtubules around two central ones
nine evenly spaced triplets of microtubules
questions.explanation: A centriole has nine peripheral triplet fibrils and no central tubules (9+0).

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The axoneme of cilia and flagella shows the arrangement
questions.explanation: Nine peripheral doublets surround two central singlet microtubules.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Cells of the adrenal cortex, which make steroid hormones, would be expected to have abundant
questions.explanation: SER is the site of lipid and steroid synthesis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: In a chloroplast, the chlorophyll pigments are located in the
questions.explanation: Thylakoids of the grana carry the photosynthetic pigments.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Describe the structure of a chloroplast.
questions.answer: A chloroplast has a double membrane envelope enclosing the stroma, which contains DNA, ribosomes and enzymes; inside are flattened thylakoids stacked into grana and joined by stroma lamellae. Chlorophyll is in the thylakoid membranes.
questions.explanation: The chloroplast is the site of photosynthesis.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Why do lipid-soluble substances cross the plasma membrane more easily than ions?
questions.answer: The plasma membrane has a lipid bilayer, so non-polar, lipid-soluble substances dissolve in it and pass through; polar molecules and ions are repelled by the hydrophobic core and need carrier or channel proteins.
questions.explanation: This makes the membrane selectively permeable.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Fats are esters of fatty acids with
questions.explanation: A triglyceride is made of glycerol joined to three fatty acids.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The pentose sugar present in RNA is
questions.explanation: RNA contains ribose; DNA contains 2-deoxyribose.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Starch forms a blue colour when treated with
questions.explanation: Iodine is held in the helical starch molecule, producing a blue-black colour.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Nucleotides in a nucleic acid strand are linked together by
questions.explanation: The phosphate group links the 3' carbon of one sugar and the 5' carbon of the next.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Enzymes are usually stored at low temperature rather than at high temperature, because low temperature
options: temporarily reduces activity but preserves the structure
questions.explanation: High temperature denatures enzymes; low temperature only slows them, and the effect is reversible.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The number of peptide bonds in a polypeptide chain of 150 amino acids is
questions.explanation: A linear chain of n amino acids has n minus 1 peptide bonds.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Describe the structure of a nucleotide and how a polynucleotide chain is formed.
questions.answer: A nucleotide is a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar and a phosphate group. Nucleotides join through phosphodiester bonds between the phosphate of one and the sugar of the next, forming a polynucleotide.
questions.explanation: DNA and RNA are polynucleotides.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Using the idea of the transition state, explain how an enzyme speeds up a reaction.
questions.answer: The substrate must reach a high-energy transition state before turning into product, which needs activation energy. The enzyme binds the substrate at its active site and stabilises the transition state, lowering the energy barrier so the reaction is faster, but the energy difference between substrate and product is unchanged.
questions.explanation: Enzymes do not change the equilibrium.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The phase of the cell cycle that follows mitosis and precedes DNA replication is
questions.explanation: The interphase order is G1, S, G2.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: In animal cells, the spindle apparatus is organised by the
questions.explanation: The centrosome with its centrioles organises the microtubules of the spindle.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The X-shaped structures called chiasmata become visible in the stage of
questions.explanation: In diplotene the homologues separate partially but stay held at chiasmata.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: If the amount of DNA in a G1 cell is 2C, the amount in the same cell at G2 is
questions.explanation: DNA doubles in the S phase, and the chromosome number stays the same.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: A diploid cell has 2C DNA in G1. The DNA content of each cell at the end of meiosis I is
questions.explanation: After replication the cell has 4C; meiosis I halves it to 2C per cell, and meiosis II to C.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The stage of meiotic prophase I that ends with the breakdown of the nuclear envelope and the nucleolus, and has terminalisation of chiasmata, is
questions.explanation: Diakinesis is the last stage of prophase I, just before metaphase I.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: State the significance of mitosis.
questions.answer: Mitosis keeps the chromosome number constant in daughter cells; it allows growth of the organism, replacement of old or damaged cells and, in plants, continuous growth by meristems.
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces genetically identical cells.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Give three differences between mitosis and meiosis.
questions.answer: Mitosis occurs in somatic cells and has one division giving two identical diploid cells with no crossing over; meiosis occurs in germ cells, has two divisions, gives four haploid cells and includes crossing over.
keyPoints: Two diploid or four haploid cells
questions.explanation: Meiosis creates variation and halves chromosome number.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which of the following is a C4 plant?
questions.explanation: Maize, sugarcane and sorghum are C4 plants.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The metal present in the chlorophyll molecule is
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll has a porphyrin head with a magnesium atom at the centre.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The water-splitting complex of photosystem II requires which of these ions?
questions.explanation: Manganese is needed for the oxygen-evolving complex, along with Cl- and Ca2+.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The regeneration of RuBP, the CO2 acceptor, in the Calvin cycle requires
questions.explanation: Regeneration needs one ATP for phosphorylation of ribulose-5-phosphate.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: Which plants show a higher rate of photosynthesis at high temperature and high light intensity?
questions.explanation: C4 plants have a higher temperature optimum and no photorespiration loss.

questions.subject: biology
questions.q: The number of ATP molecules required in the Calvin cycle for making one molecule of glucose is
questions.explanation: Each CO2 needs 3 ATP, so 6 CO2 need 18 ATP (and 12 NADPH).
